messages.subject: [Bioc-sig-proteomics] Welcome to bioc-sig-proteomics
messages.body_plain:
Dear subscribers,

This mailing list has been set up following the Bioconductor developer
meeting in Heidelberg [1,2], where some developers interested in
analysing proteomics data agreed to combine their efforts to develop
'tools for the analysis and comprehension of proteomics
high-throughput data'. Things being as there are, not very much has
happened since then, but hopefully this list will become a place to
share and discuss current and future development. You are welcome to
post your own interest/ideas/work. Do also feel free to also post
questions about data analysis in parallel to the main Bioc mailing
list.

Best wishes,

Laurent

[1] http://www-huber.embl.de/biocdeveleurope2010/
[2] http://bioconductor.org/help/course-materials/2010/HeidelbergNovember2010/


--
Laurent Gatto
Cambridge Centre For Proteomics
http://www.bio.cam.ac.uk/proteomics

messages.subject: [Bioc-sig-proteomics] MSnbase package
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

MSnbase is a Bioconductor package that provides base functions and
classes for MS-based proteomics. Current functionality is raw spectra
plotting, data manipulation, data processing and quantification of
labelled mass spectrometry experiments (using iTRAQ or TMT reporter
tags). Version 1.0.1 is available for R/Bioc stable [1], but multiple
improvements have already been added (and will be on a regular basis)
in the devel version [2]. Two vignettes are available: one that
describes MSnbase's functionality and one that describes underlying
classes. MSnbase has been developed using the Biobase's classes as
model to allow best compatibility with existing infrastructure.

If you have questions and/or suggestions, please do not hesitate to
contact me directly or share your thoughts on the mailing list.

Best wishes,

Laurent

[1] http://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/MSnbase.html
[2] http://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/html/MSnbase.html



-- 
Laurent Gatto
Cambridge Centre For Proteomics
http://www.bio.cam.ac.uk/proteomics
